messages.text: What did Pocognoli change in first Scotland game in charge?

metadata.summary: A draw might not be the most inspiring result for a new era, but there were still plenty of positives for Sebastien Pocognoli to take from his first game in charge of Scotland.
metadata.content: Slovenia 0-0 Scotland: What did Sebastien Pocognoli change in first game as Scottish boss since replacing Steve Clarke? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Slovenia 0-0 Scotland: What did Sebastien Pocognoli change in first game as Scottish boss since replacing Steve Clarke? Scotland drew 0-0 with Slovenia in Sebastien Pocognoli's first game in charge; it is the first time Scotland haven't been led by Steve Clarke since 2019; despite failing to win, there were plenty of positives for Pocognoli to take from the game Callum Bishop Football Journalist Saturday 26 September 2026 18:14, UK Image: Sebastien Pocognoli's Scotland showed promising signs in 0-0 draw with Slovenia A draw might not be the most inspiring result for a new era, but there were still plenty of positives for Sebastien Pocognoli to take from his first game in charge of Scotland. On the surface, 0-0 against Slovenia doesn't exactly scream entertaining. On another day though, Scotland could've either won by four or lost by a couple; such was the nature of the contest. In the first half they looked vulnerable, but the second completely dominant. So, what exactly did Pocognoli do to change things up for the better, and what does he still need to keep his eye on? messages.text: 'I was driving like my grandma' - Antonelli admits to lack of confidence

metadata.summary: World championship leader Kimi Antonelli says he was driving "like his grandmother" during the Azerbaijan Grand Prix because of a lack of confidence at the Baku City Circuit.
metadata.content: Kimi Antonelli: F1 championship leader says he was 'driving like his grandma' due to lack of confidence at Azerbaijan GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Kimi Antonelli: F1 championship leader says he was 'driving like his grandma' due to lack of confidence at Azerbaijan GP Kimi Antonelli's world champions lead over George Russell was reduced to 66 points following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix; Antonelli recovered from 16th on the grid to finish fifth, while Russel won from pole position Saturday 26 September 2026 16:46, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli says that the Azerbaijan GP was 'one of those days you have to be happy with P5' but adds that he will be 'back at my level' at the Malaysian Grand Prix. World championship leader Kimi Antonelli says he was driving "like his grandmother" during the Azerbaijan Grand Prix because of a lack of confidence at the Baku City Circuit. Antonelli staged a decent recovery in Saturday's race to come from 16th on the grid, following a crash in qualifying, to finish fifth, but his championship lead over his Mercedes team-mate George Russell was reduced to 66 points as the Brit claimed victory. The 20-year-old Italian has shown remarkable consistency to build a commanding lead at the top of the standings, but struggled in Baku after missing a significant chunk of practice due to technical issues with his car. messages.text: Pierre Royal strikes Cambridgeshire gold for Ireland

metadata.summary: Pierre Royal got his nose in front when it mattered most in the dying strides to land the bet365 Cambridgeshire at Newmarket.
metadata.content: Pierre Royal strikes Cambridgeshire gold for Ireland | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Pierre Royal strikes Cambridgeshire gold for Ireland A first trip to Newmarket was a winning one for Adrian McGuinness as the only Irish raider Pierre Royal struck gold in the coveted Cambridgeshire Handicap. Saturday 26 September 2026 16:55, UK Image: Winning connections with jockey Mikey Sheehy and Pierre Royal after winning the bet365 Cambridgeshire Pierre Royal got his nose in front when it mattered most in the dying strides to land the bet365 Cambridgeshire at Newmarket. But connections of the Adrian McGuinness-trained four-year-old had a tense wait before the judge confirmed he had edged Crest Of Fire to become the first Irish-trained winner of the race this century. Both the winner and second came from the group on the far side and it was Jack Channon's Crest Of Fire who was first to emerge in the hands of Tom Marquand. But he was stalked all the way by the Mikey Sheehy-ridden Pierre Royal and the 33-1 shot reeled him to just get up. messages.text: 'Some drivers that shouldn't be in F1' - Norris calls for Colapinto race ban

metadata.summary: Lando Norris said Franco Colapinto should receive a race ban for the collision that wiped him and Pierre Gasly out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Lando Norris: McLaren driver calls for Franco Colapinto race ban after Azerbaijan GP three-car collision with Alpines | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lando Norris: McLaren driver calls for Franco Colapinto race ban after Azerbaijan GP three-car collision with Alpines Franco Colapinto apologetic for the "big mistake" that saw him cause chain reaction collision with team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris, forcing all three to retire; Colapinto to serve grid drop at Bahrain GP; Norris says "just some drivers that shouldn't be in Formula 1" Saturday 26 September 2026 17:28, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player There was carnage on the safety car restart after contact between Alpine team-mates resulted in Lando Norris crashing out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Lando Norris said Franco Colapinto should receive a race ban for the collision that wiped him and Pierre Gasly out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. At the first Safety Car restart on lap 36, Colapinto badly misjudged his braking into the first corner and, carrying too much speed, steamed into the side of Alpine team-mate Gasly, whose car was sent into Norris' McLaren on its outside. Norris was spun into the barriers, with the two Alpines also forced to retire with damage. Gasly had been running seventh, Norris eighth and Colapinto 10th. messages.text: Sun Goddess passes 'massive test' to rule supreme in Cheveley Park

metadata.summary: Sun Goddess showed her class to give Aidan O'Brien a seventh Tattersalls Sceptre Sessions Cheveley Park Stakes in what was an appropriately red-hot renewal at Newmarket.
metadata.content: Sun Goddess passes 'massive test' to rule supreme in Cheveley Park | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sun Goddess passes 'massive test' to rule supreme in Cheveley Park Aidan O'Brien's star filly Sun Goddess recorded a third Group One success with an emphatic display in the Cheveley Park Stakes, in a record-setting time. Saturday 26 September 2026 16:16, UK Image: Ryan Moore on Sun Goddess wins the Tattersalls Sceptre Sessions Cheveley Park Stakes Sun Goddess showed her class to give Aidan O'Brien a seventh Tattersalls Sceptre Sessions Cheveley Park Stakes in what was an appropriately red-hot renewal at Newmarket. Sun Goddess and fellow Group One heroine Senorita Bonita travelled in tandem in midfield as Snowing and Moonrise set a strong pace up the six furlongs of the Rowley Mile. Senorita Bonita was the first to show her hand, with the smooth-travelling Libertango launching her attack under Billy Loughnane on the far side from the back of the field. But Sun Goddess found plenty for Ryan Moore on meeting the rising ground, with the 5-6 favourite engaging top gear to win by a going-away length from Libertango, making it her third top-level win of the campaign. Senorita Bonita was only able to finish fifth after not getting home. messages.text: Fitzpatrick builds big lead at Open de France as Fleetwood withdraws

metadata.summary: Matt Fitzpatrick moved a big step closer to a fourth worldwide win of the season after taking a five-shot lead into the final round of the FedEx Open de France.
metadata.content: Open de France: England's Matt Fitzpatrick takes five-shot lead into final day as Tommy Fleetwood withdraws with illness | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Open de France: England's Matt Fitzpatrick takes five-shot lead into final day as Tommy Fleetwood withdraws with illness Matt Fitzpatrick heads into the final day on 19 under and five clear of France's Tom Vaillant; Fitzpatrick has carded just one bogey over the first three days at Le Golf National; watch the final round live on Sunday from 11.30am on Sky Sports Golf Saturday 26 September 2026 17:59, UK Image: Matt Fitzpatrick has built a big lead at the FedEx Open de France Matt Fitzpatrick moved a big step closer to a fourth worldwide win of the season after taking a five-shot lead into the final round of the FedEx Open de France. The Englishman held a one-shot advantage heading into the weekend at Le Golf National but pulled further ahead with a six-under 65 on Saturday afternoon, mixing seven birdies with his first bogey of the week. Fitzpatrick - already a winner on the PGA Tour at the Valspar Championship, RBC Heritage and Zurich Classic of New Orleans this year - moved to 19 under and with a commanding advantage over France's Tom Vaillant.
